uses.argument: A no-feedback codeword pair is a deterministic function of the finite message pair. The whole Gaussian noise vector is independent of the messages, hence of the entire input-shift vector; unconditional finite-mixture entropies and density-ratio integrability require no new hypothesis.

For S={1}, condition on (M2,Y^{i-1}); X2i is known and subtracted. X1i is a function of M1. Fresh Zi is independent of the sigma-algebra generated by (M1,M2,Z^{i-1}), which contains both X1i and (M2,Y^{i-1}). Thus Zi is independent of that entire pair. The reflected argument handles S={2}.

Conditioning variable is Y^{i-1}, input shift is X1i+X2i. Both are measurable functions of messages and previous noises. Fresh Zi is independent of that joint sigma-algebra. Average input second moments are finite by the code power budgets, giving the required conditional finite moments and entropy integrability.

uses.argument: Each current encoder input is measurable in its own message and Y^{i-1}. The pair of current inputs and any conditioning made from messages/history is measurable in (M1,M2,Z^{i-1}). The current normalized unit Gaussian noise is independent of this whole sigma-algebra, so every conditional finite mixture is a genuine Gaussian convolution. Finite average powers bound average conditional moments.

For the first user the side variable is (M2,Y^{i-1}); V2i is known and subtracted, while the signal is V1i. Both that signal and the side variable are measurable in messages and past noises, independent jointly of current Zi. Zero conditional variance produces a translated Gaussian with finite entropy and is already explicitly split.

Signal is V1i+V2i and side variable is Y^{i-1}; both belong to the past/message sigma-algebra independent of fresh Zi. The strengthened scalar conditional convolution bound therefore applies exactly, with average variance subsequently bounded by unconditional variance.
